note: Hand-written with the help of an AI coding assistant (Claude) and reviewed by the author. texts: one background post per group, month of year and year covered; replies: comment pool used without repeats; descriptions: past events by group and local start date.

10: Carpool from the north end has two seats.
Winter program pieces get handed out tonight. Please take only the copies for your voice part.
11: Practice tracks for the winter pieces are up. The alto track for the third piece was redone, so grab the new one.
12: Thank you all for a wonderful concert.
01: Rehearsal is in the side chapel this week.
First rehearsal of the year is January 6. Bring a pencil, we are marking breaths in the new pieces.
02: Sheet music for the spring program is in the folders.
Spring sing-along is March 14. Feel free to bring a friend or two, songbooks provided.
03: Please practice measures 40 to 60 at home.
If the Latin is giving you trouble, there is a pronunciation guide taped inside the back cover of your folder.
04: Lost: a black folder with alto parts.
Hall heat was off tonight. The office says it will be fixed by next week, but bring a sweater just in case.
05: We counted about 120 in the hall Saturday. The bake sale covered the cost of the new folders.
06: Recordings from Tuesday are on the shared page.
Summer schedule: rehearsals run 7 to 8:30 through August, and no sectionals until fall.
07: Does anyone have a box fan we could borrow for the hall? It gets stuffy by the second hour.
08: The piano was tuned on Monday.
The fall folders need new labels. If you own a label maker, please bring it Tuesday.
09: Concert dress is black on black.
Fall term dues can go in the envelope on the music stand. Talk to the treasurer if you need more time.

10: Mind the ice by the north gate.
Costume parade is the 24th at 11. You can bring up to three guests.
11: New bench donated by the Mosses.
Dark by 5 now and the path light by the back fence is out. Bring a flashlight.
12: Happy holidays from the dog park.
01: Frost on the agility ramp this morning and it was slick. Walked mine around it.
02: Gate latch is sticky, push hard.
Someone left a blue thermos on the bench by the fountain. It is hanging on the fence.
03: Puddles by the benches, wear boots.
The city put gravel down by the entrance where the mud was worst. Big improvement.
04: Spring cleanup is April 18 at 9. One guest each is fine, rakes and gloves provided.
05: Small dog area is closed for reseeding.
Lots of foxtails along the back fence right now. Check paws and ears when you get home.
06: Found a red collar near the gate.
Shade sail is back up over the benches.
07: Please fill the holes your dogs dig.
The pavement by the gate gets too hot for paws in the afternoon. Mornings and evenings are better.
08: Heard a couple of dogs have kennel cough. If yours is coughing, please keep them home for a week or two.
09: Leaves are piling up in the small dog area. If you have ten spare minutes and a rake, it helps.

10: Ridge Road is covered in wet leaves. Take the descents slow.
11: One ride a week until spring, Sundays at 8 from the shop.
01: Cold one this Sunday. Booties and a wind vest recommended, we will keep the stops short.
02: Road work on Ridge Road, detour posted.
The shop is doing club member tune-ups at a discount through the end of the month.
03: Lights on for the evening ride.
Season opener is March 21 from the shop. Members only, three pace groups.
04: Flat tire clinic at the shop on Thursday.
Pollen is bad on the lakeshore stretch. Wear glasses even if it is cloudy.
05: Planning on the Lakeshore 40? Come to a Saturday ride first and practice riding in a pace line.
06: Lakeshore 40 went great. 26 finishers and nobody missed the turn at the boat ramp.
07: Heat advisory for Saturday, so the ride moves up to 6:30.
08: Gravel route is muddy, bring fenders.
Smoke is heavy today. Sunday ride is canceled, we will check the air again Saturday night.
09: Who is in for the century?
Century practice ride is the 19th. About 70 miles, two stops, rolling at 7.

10: Leftover sale books are boxed up for the senior center. Pickup is Tuesday morning.
11: Holiday sale prices: paperbacks a dollar, hardcovers two, kids books three for a dollar.
01: New picture books are on the cart.
Tax forms are in the rack by the entrance this year, not at the desk.
02: Book sale donations go in the bins by the desk.
Book sale is February 7. If you signed up for setup, we start at 8.
03: Someone donated a full set of old encyclopedias. We cannot sell them, so speak up soon if you want them.
04: Spring cleaning? We take hardcovers and paperbacks in good shape. No textbooks or magazines, please.
05: The returns slot is jammed, use the desk.
The seed library is back by the windows. Take a few packets and bring some back in the fall.
06: Story time moves to the big room this month.
Summer reading kickoff is the 27th in the children's room. Each family can bring two guests.
07: Air conditioning in the community room is out, so donation sorting moves to the back office for now.
08: Back to school book bags are at the front desk this week. One per family.
09: Thank you for a great book sale.
Need a few strong backs to carry boxes up from the storeroom before the October sale.

descriptions.g-library|2025-02-08: Volunteer shifts for the winter sale, twelve spots in all. Wear layers, the community room stays cold until the heat kicks in, and the small lot fills fast, so street parking is easier.
descriptions.g-dogpark|2025-02-22: First cleanup of the year. We will clear branches from the winter storms and fill the low spots by the fountain. Gloves and bags provided, one guest per member, and dogs are better off at home for this one.
descriptions.g-choir|2025-03-15: Come sing with us, no experience needed. Songbooks are handed out at the door and there is tea and cookies at the break. Up to two guests per member, kids welcome.
descriptions.g-cycling|2025-03-22: Our first group ride of the season, about 25 miles with a short cut for anyone who wants it. Members only. Pump your tires before you come and bring a spare tube; the ride leader goes over hand signals at 7:50.
descriptions.g-dogpark|2025-04-19: Raking, weeding the fence line and fresh wood chips for the small dog area. If it pours we push to the next Saturday. One guest per member.
descriptions.g-library|2025-04-26: A local author reads from her new mystery, set in a town a lot like ours, then takes questions. Seating tops out at 50, so one guest each. Copies will be for sale at the desk.
descriptions.g-choir|2025-05-10: The spring program runs about an hour with one intermission. Free to attend, and donations go toward new sheet music. Members can hold up to four guest seats; the church lot opens at 6:30.
descriptions.g-cycling|2025-05-31: Forty miles around the lake at a steady pace, with a water stop at the halfway turnaround. Members only. The trailhead lot is small, so carpool or ride over, and helmets are required.
descriptions.g-choir|2025-06-21: Light summer songs outdoors at the bandstand. Bring a blanket or a folding chair. Rain moves us into the church hall, and you can bring up to three guests.
descriptions.g-library|2025-06-28: Kids pick up their reading logs and a free book to start the summer, and there is a short puppet show at 11. Children need a spot too, and each member can add two guests.
descriptions.g-dogpark|2025-07-12: Kiddie pools, sprinklers and a lot of wet dogs. Bring a towel and maybe a change of shoes for yourself. Dogs must be current on shots; two guests per member.
descriptions.g-cycling|2025-08-16: Repeats on Ridge Road, as many as you like, turning at the top each time. Capped at 20 riders, members only. Bring two bottles, it warms up fast once the sun clears the hill.
descriptions.g-choir|2025-09-13: Morning meeting to start the fall term: music handout, voice checks for new singers and a short rehearsal. Members only. Coffee and pastries from 9:45.
descriptions.g-cycling|2025-10-04: Easy social ride out past the orchards and back, roughly 30 miles with a coffee stop. Members only. It is chilly at the start, so bring a layer that fits in a jersey pocket.
descriptions.g-library|2025-10-04: Twelve volunteer spots for the fall sale across setup, cashier and pack-up. Comfortable shoes and a water bottle help. Members only; message the sale coordinator if you need to swap shifts.
descriptions.g-dogpark|2025-10-25: Costume parade around the big field at 11:30, with small prizes for funniest and most homemade. Leave the candy at home, chocolate is dangerous for dogs. Up to three guests per member.
descriptions.g-library|2025-12-06: Winter stories, a snowflake craft and cocoa in the children's room. Each child takes a spot, and members can bring up to two guests. Stroller parking is by the back door.
descriptions.g-choir|2025-12-13: Carols, a few new pieces and a singalong to close the night. Admission is free and the bake sale table helps pay for the hall. Up to four guest seats per member, doors at 6:30.
descriptions.g-dogpark|2025-12-13: A volunteer with a good camera takes holiday portraits by the big tree, free, with photos emailed the week after. Bring a squeaky toy to get your dog looking up. Two guests per member.
descriptions.g-library|2026-02-07: We need twelve volunteers for the winter sale. The cash box and price signs are in the storeroom, and the book sale coordinator will walk first timers through checkout. Members only.
descriptions.g-choir|2026-03-14: This year it is all songs from musicals, with the words on a screen so nobody has to read music. Two guests per member. The hall is step free from the side door.
descriptions.g-cycling|2026-03-21: Shake off the winter legs with a flat 20 miles, regrouping at every turn. Members only. The shop opens early for a quick air check, and we roll at 8 sharp.
descriptions.g-dogpark|2026-04-18: Work day at the north gate. This spring we are patching the fence line and painting the benches, so wear clothes you do not mind ruining. One guest each, donuts at 10.
descriptions.g-choir|2026-05-09: Spring program with a few new arrangements and a guest pianist in the second half. Free, with a donation basket by the door, and up to four guests per member. Singers warm up at 6:15 in the side chapel.
descriptions.g-cycling|2026-06-13: Second year for this one: 40 miles around the lake with a rest stop run by club volunteers. Members only, 30 riders max. If thunderstorms are forecast, the ride leaders will post a go or no go by 6 that morning.
descriptions.g-library|2026-06-27: Sign up for summer reading, get your log and pick out a free paperback. A neighbor with a guitar plays a few songs at 10:45. Two guests per member, and children count toward the 40 spots.
descriptions.g-dogpark|2026-07-11: Pools, a sprinkler and frozen treats, plus a separate splash corner for small dogs. Check the supplies sheet if you can lend a pool or towels. Two guests per member; dogs that dislike water stay leashed near the pools.
descriptions.g-choir|2026-09-12: Fall term starts here. We will hand out the winter music, collect dues and read through two pieces. Members only, and new singers should come at 9:30 for a quick range check.
descriptions.g-cycling|2026-09-19: A 70 mile practice for anyone eyeing a century, with stops at miles 25 and 50 and a sweeper at the back. Members only, 25 riders max. Bring food you know your stomach can handle.
descriptions.g-library|2026-10-03: Fall sale volunteers, twelve spots across three shifts. Pack-up is always the hardest to fill, so if you have a car, please consider it. Members only; questions go to the book sale coordinator.
descriptions.g-dogpark|2026-10-24: Year two of the parade. Judging starts at 11:30, and there is a new category for matching owner and dog costumes. Up to three guests each, and keep costumes clear of eyes and noses.
